title: find-contacts record
description: One record per company, always emitted, so a company that returned nothing is distinguishable from one that was never run.

domain.description: Registrable domain, no scheme. Used for deduplication.

audience.description: Free text, matched downstream against offer.variants[].audience in the seller profile. Absent means the default offer applies.

status.description: ok = target met. partial = fewer people or signals than asked for. failed = nothing usable. A failed record is still a record.

notes.description: Why a record is partial or failed, in one line.

researched_at.description: Date the research ran, YYYY-MM-DD. Taken from the environment at run start, never hardcoded.

recency_window_months.description: What 'recent' meant for this run, so a later reader can judge staleness.

people.description: Verified decision-makers. May be empty; an empty array with status partial or failed is an honest answer.

recipient_id.description: Stable id, minted here as R-0001 upward. The resume key for every downstream step.

profile_url.description: A checkable public page showing this person in this role. A professional network profile, a company leadership page, a dated press release or a conference speaker page all qualify. Omit the person entirely if you cannot find one.

profile_source.description: What kind of page profile_url is, e.g. 'company leadership page'.

persona_match.description: Honest self-report against the declared buyer. Sorting a finished run by fallback is how you discover your buyer definition was too vague.

why_right_contact.description: Which declared title rule or persona clause this person satisfies. 'Senior leader at the company' is a failure, not a justification.

role_status.description: conflicting means two sources disagree. Flag it rather than silently picking one.

role_source_url.description: The dated primary source, where one exists.

signals.description: Dated, sourced events. Ranked by the seller profile's signal_priority.

fact.description: What happened, one sentence, as the source states it.

date.description: YYYY-MM at minimum. Undated pages are the single most common trap; establish the actual year before using a signal.

type.description: Free text, drawn from the seller profile's signal_priority ladder.

source_url.description: The page that states it. Not a search result page.

angle.description: One line: how this seller's offer connects to this event, in the seller's own terms. Never a booking link and never a call to action.

evidence_url.description: Sourcing step only. A page that names this company. Required there; a candidate without one is dropped.

fit_score.description: Sourcing step only. Judged from the company's own words, not a directory blurb.

fit_reason.description: Sourcing step only. One line, in their own words.

liveness.description: Sourcing step. What happened when the domain was checked. A label, not a gate: a company is not dropped for a site that would not load.

site_count.description: Sourcing step. How many register entries this one organisation covers. Registers list premises; you are selling to the organisation.

registers.description: Sourcing step. Which register or registers listed this organisation. Two independent registers is a stronger signal than one.
